opening.argument: The speaker is shopping for yard supplies and then doing lawn work. They describe going to Lowe's with a five-dollar gift card, discuss a mulch price, and report buying discounted landscape fabric. The footage shows mulch in a vehicle and mulch spread around the house, grounding those purchases in the landscaping work shown. The coupon reference does not turn that account into a deceptive transaction: the description questions whether the reported offer still works and says people trying to obtain gift cards at checkout found it was not working. Those limitations matter. The observable activity is ordinary retail shopping and yard work, while the reported promotion is presented with doubt rather than an assured result.

citations.quote: I'm heading to my Lowe's because I did get my little gift card only five dollars
I purchased these rolls of landscape fabric from Dollar Generalist here and they had it at 90% off paying 50 cents per roll.
I had people in checkout texting for their gift card and it wasn't working then
